column19: The four (4) monitors identified above are used for federal compliance and maintained by the State Environmental Agency TCEQ. The TCEQ uses a variety of measures to ensure its air monitoring data is of the utmost quality. Air monitors are assessed daily to verify their operations remain within proper specifications. TCEQ personnel physically visit each monitoring station on a weekly basis to conduct various quality control checks and preventive maintenance activities. The monitoring instruments themselves must meet rigorous sampling and analytical requirements prescribed by federal air monitoring rules and undergo daily, weekly, and quarterly quality control checks to verify the instrument's calibration, accuracy, and precision. In addition, independently calibrated instruments are used to perform quarterly and annual audits of the air monitors and their operation. Finally, a validation assessment is performed on all data to verify the TCEQ's data quality objectives are met. The data are reviewed for outliers, regional comparability, quality assurance/quality control requirements, and other data quality assessment indicators. Data that do not meet these objectives completely are invalidated or denoted accordingly. The City also collaborates with local University of Texas researchers and the Capital Area Council of Governments (CAPCOG) for localized monitoring using Purple Air monitors, which provide live results at https://map.purpleair.com/

Before 2024, PM10 sampling only occurred once every six days, but beginning in 2024, a continuous PM10 monitor was added to the Austin Audubon site which recorded daily PM10 values. The region recorded nine days when O3 levels were considered “unhealthy for sensitive groups” and five days when PM2.5 levels were considered “unhealthy for sensitive groups”. In additional there were 183 days when either O3 or PM2.5 levels were considered “moderate,” or worse, 45 days when it was “moderate” or worse for both O3 and PM2.5, and 9 days considered “moderate” or worse for both PM10 and PM2.5.

column19: In 2017, Toronto published \'Avoiding the TRAP: Traffic-Related Air Pollution in Toronto and Options for Reducing Exposure\'. City-wide air quality study results indicate that some traffic-related air pollutants (TRAPs), benzene and PM10, are present at levels that may exceed the health benchmarks set by the federal Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change (MOECC) at times in Toronto. AAQCs and Canada-Wide Standards (CWSs) are benchmarks that represent an upper limit of desirable concentrations of contaminants in air, and are intended to be protective of health and/or environmental effects. In local (neighbourhood-level) air quality studies, benzene, benzo[a]pyrene, PM10, and PM2.5 - all of which are important vehicle emissions - were identified as exceeding the relevant health benchmarks. The city-wide modelling also suggests that additional substances may exceed AAQCs in some parts of Toronto, including cadmium, chromium, and vinyl chloride.\n\nSee report for details: https://www.toronto.ca/legdocs/mmis/2017/hl/bgrd/backgroundfile-108070.pdf

Change of the index as of January 1, 2021

Since 1994, the Approved Associations for Air Quality Monitoring (AASQA), including Airparif for the Île-de-France region, have been publishing a daily air quality indicator, the ATMO index, calculated for urban areas with a population of over 100,000, based on the concentrations in the air of four regulated pollutants: sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), ozone (O3), and particles with a diameter of less than 10 µm (PM10).Since 2011, they have also been publishing the index of European cities, Citeair (developed through a European project coordinated by Airparif).The ATMO index has not undergone major changes since its creation. However, considering the public health issue represented by air quality and the need for more comprehensive information expressed by the population, a revision of the index has become necessary. Thanks to the improvement of monitoring tools, it has become possible to provide personalized and geolocated information.The evolution of the index, adopted by the Ministry of Ecological Transition, is based on several innovations:It incorporates a new regulated pollutant: fine particles PM2.5, with proven health effects. Its thresholds are aligned with those chosen by the European Environment Agency;•The scale also evolves: the 'Very Good' level disappears, and the 'Extremely Bad' level is introduced. The new index therefore classifies air quality into 6 categories: Good / Moderate / Poor / Bad / Very Bad / Extremely Bad;•The color range now extends from blue (good) to magenta (extremely bad);•It provides a forecast calculated at the level of each inter-municipal public institution (EPCI), across the entire national territory, including overseas. It thus provides a finer indication of the population's exposure to air pollution, with information at different territorial scales, from the EPCI to geolocation; these new features in the calculation of the ATMO index make it more representative of the state of air quality, while being more in line with the expectations of citizens. It can be applied at a finer spatial scale.
(https://www.paris.fr/pages/etat-des-lieux-de-la-qualite-de-l-air-a-paris-7101)

According to AirParif, in 2024, the center of Paris had 7 days rated 'bad' regarding the Atmo Index.
(https://www.airparif.fr/surveiller-la-pollution/historique-des-indices)

O monitoramento da qualidade do ar é aferido através do SOPRAR/Salvador, uma ferramenta de mapeamento da qualidade do ar, que considera os aspectos físicos e dinâmicos que regem o transporte de poluentes atmosféricos resultando em concentrações nocivas. O sistema está operacionalizado na infraestrutura computacional da Plataforma de Bioinformática do IGM-FIOCRUZ e pode ser acessado através de um serviço WEB exclusivo. Baseia-se em uma cadeia de modelos numéricos atmosféricos (WRF-CHIMERE) que representam os processos físico-químicos, a meteorologia e a dispersão dos poluentes na área de interesse. O modelo meteorológico WRF é processado pelo CEMADEC e transferido para o servidor que hospeda o SOPRAR/Salvador via protocolo FTP. As simulações de transporte e química atmosférica (CHIMERE) são processadas diariamente produzindo mapas de previsão de concentrações de seis poluentes diferentes, incluindo material particulado inalável fino (PM2.5) e ozônio (O3), além de indicadores de qualidade do ar (baseados na metodologia da CETESB) para as próximas 48h com resolução de 3km.

On days in which ground-level ozone and/or fine particulate matter (PM2. 5) are at unhealthy levels for sensitive groups or above, the Office of Sustainability will call a “Knozone Action Day” for the Central Indiana region. On these days the Office of Sustainability will work with media to disseminate communication around the risks of spending extended time outdoors due to poor air quality, especially as it relates to those most vulnerable. Residents are also urged to take action by choosing a cleaner commute, avoiding idling, and spreading the word to family and friends. Goyang Special City (Mayor Lee Dong-hwan) is implementing the '2024 Small Business Air Pollution Prevention Facility Installation Support Project' targeting small and medium-sized enterprises that emit air pollutants, in order to improve air quality and reduce fine dust. The budget for this project in 2024 is a total of 590 million won.
Additionally, Goyang City will support 90% of the costs for installing and replacing outdated pollution prevention facilities at small-scale air emission businesses, to reduce air pollutants such as dust, sulfur oxides, and nitrogen oxides, and to alleviate the economic burden on businesses. Especially, as the installation of Internet of Things (IoT) measuring devices for real-time operation information of air emission facilities and prevention facilities at 4-5 types of businesses will become mandatory by June 30, 2025, the city is prioritizing support for the cost of attaching these measuring devices. Goyang City selected some of the target facilities for prevention facilities and IoT installation through the first announcement on March 1, and is currently conducting a second announcement for the remaining IoT installation budget. Businesses wishing to receive IoT installation support can refer to the announcements on the Goyang City website or the Gyeonggi Environmental and Energy Promotion Agency website to apply.
Meanwhile, since 2019, the city has invested approximately 4.7 billion won to support the installation and replacement costs of outdated air pollution prevention facilities such as dust collectors at 99 businesses.
Goyang City will make every effort to achieve the carbon reduction targets for 2030.

REMAH Red de Monitoreo Ambiental de Hermosillo

REMAH is the result of joint work between academics and students from the Universidad de Sonora and the Municipal Agency for Energy and Climate Change (AMECC). The project is part of the activities of the TEAMS group (Advanced Electric Transport and Sustainable Mobility Group), which aims to improve air quality in the cities of Hermosillo and Cuernavaca.

Sensor Network

The air quality monitoring network of the Municipal Agency for Energy and Climate Change of Hermosillo (AMECCH) includes 10 sensors located in different areas of the city. Readings are taken every five minutes and stored on a server, where the data analysis team can access the information and display it on consultation maps. An additional five sensors will be added to the network as part of the TEAMS project in collaboration with El Colegio de Sonora and the Universidad de Sonora.

column19: Material Particulado de 10 micrones (PM10) período corto (20 minutos): el material particulado (MP) hace referencia a partículas inhalables que pueden ser de diferente tamaño y generalmente se definen por su diámetro aerodinámico. Las principales fuentes pueden tener diferentes orígenes, pero generalmente incluyen actividades domésticas, tráfico y transporte, actividades industriales, plantas de energía, sitios de construcción, quema de desechos e incendios. Se utiliza como indicador de este contaminante el promedio anual de todas las mediciones realizadas en un período de 20 minutos durante el año analizado, y se toma como referencia el valor límite de 500 µg/m3, establecido por la Resolución Provincial 201/2004 para PM10 período corto. Las mediciones se realizan mediante un convenio realizado con la Universidad Tecnológica Nacional - Facultad Regional Rosario (UTN - FRRo), en el que se establece la realización de seis (6) monitoreos de este contaminante por mes, en distintos puntos de la ciudad definidos por la Dirección de Fiscalización Ambiental (DFA). También se promedian las mediciones en calidad de aire realizadas por las empresas que cuentan con programas de monitoreos de emisiones atmosféricas aprobados por la DFA. Se realizan en 77 estaciones distintas y 98 mediciones.

Se utiliza como indicador de este contaminante el promedio anual de todas las mediciones realizadas en un período de 30 días durante el año analizado y se toma como referencia el valor límite de 1 mg/cm2 por 30 días, establecido por la Ordenanza No. 5820/1994. Al igual que en los casos anteriores, las mediciones se realizan, mediante un convenio realizado con la UTN - FRRo, en el que se establece la realización de dieciséis (16) monitoreos de este contaminante por mes, en distintos puntos de la ciudad definidos por la DFA. También se promedian las mediciones en calidad de aire realizadas por las empresas que cuentan con programas de monitoreos de emisiones atmosféricas aprobados por la DFA. La cantidad de estaciones de monitoreo de este contaminante son 71 estaciones distintas de 145 mediciones.\n

column19: Óxidos de Nitrógeno (NOx): Los óxidos de nitrógeno son una mezcla de gases compuestos de nitrógeno y oxígeno. El término NOx hace referencia a la combinación de monóxido de nitrógeno (NO) y el dióxido de nitrógeno (NO2) ya que son los óxidos de nitrógeno más importantes desde el punto de vista toxicológico; ninguno de los dos son inflamables y son incoloros a pardo en apariencia a temperatura ambiente. Son liberados al aire por procesos del transporte y de combustión. Se utiliza como indicador de este contaminante el promedio anual de todas las mediciones realizadas en un período de 20 minutos durante el año analizado y se toma como referencia el valor límite de 400 µg/m3, establecido por la Ordenanza No. 5820/1994. Al igual que en los casos anteriores, las mediciones se realizan mediante un convenio realizado con la UTN - FRRo, en el que se establece la realización de cinco (5) monitoreos de este contaminante por mes, en distintos puntos de la ciudad definidos por la DFA. También se promedian las mediciones en calidad de aire realizadas por las empresas que cuentan con programas de monitoreos de emisiones atmosféricas aprobados por la DFA. La cantidad de estaciones de monitoreo donde se mide este contaminante son 46 estaciones distintas de 76 mediciones.

column19: Ciente da importância da atuação local, e seguindo as orientações da diretiva 2008/CE, Guimarães desenvolveu de forma pró-ativa e voluntária um Plano de Gestão da Qualidade do Ar. Além daquela que integra a rede Nacional da qualidade do Ar da resposnabilidade da Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente conjuntamente com a coordenação da CCDRn, Guimarães instalou voluntariamente, em 2023, quatro estações de monitorização da qualidade do ar e outros parâmetros climáticos de relevância, em locais de amostragem de diferentes tipologias (áreas urbanas, naturais e de conflito), que permitem a análise em tempo real de NOx, PM10, O3 e PM2,5. Isto é muito importante uma vez que o Rede nacional não considerava, para Guimarães, as medições de PM2,5. O parâmetro O3 é extremamente importante para o Indicador da Natureza e Biodiversidade. Os valores em tempo real das estações locais são integrados na Plataforma Urbana e disponibilizados qualitativamente ao cidadão. Estes dados têm permitido estudar efeitos na saúde e bem estar bem como analisar com maior rigor os efeitos de incêndios ou poeiras de África que têm afetado o País. A cada seis meses é elaborado um relatório de análise e as principais conclusões, permitem apoiar a redefinição de estratégias de comunicação.

column19: Entre 2014 e 2021, não foram registadas quaisquer excedências diárias de PM10. Em 2022, foram registadas 14 excedências e em 2023 16. Desde 2022, os Episódios de Poeira Suspensa Africana estão a ganhar relevância na região norte, com um aumento de episódios. Guimarães registou níveis elevados, o que pode ter contribuído para as excedências. Além disso, em 2022, o mesmo ano em que foram registadas excedências, a área ardida em Portugal foi a maior desde 2017 (111 000 ha), com o norte de Portugal a apresentar um forte aumento em comparação com 2021 (27 129 ha). Guimarães foi/é afetada por nuvens de fumo que, combinadas com a topografia do território, poderiam explicar parcialmente o aumento das concentrações de PM10. Com o nosso sistema de monitorização local, os dados locais têm sido utilizados para compreender os impactos dos eventos extremos, tanto dos incêndios como da poeira africana. Em 2024, os dois episódios de poeira suspensa do Norte de África que afectaram a nossa cidade, foram registados por estações locais com uma equipa que os analisou para reforçar, localmente, os programas de sensibilização da Agência Nacional de Saúde. Também em setembro de 2024, como deve saber, vários incêndios de grandes dimensões na região Norte afectaram a qualidade do ar em Portugal, tendo o Governo português declarado o estado de calamidade devido ao descontrolo dos incêndios em certas regiões. Em particular, vários incêndios afectaram Guimarães, influenciando negativamente a qualidade do ar com AGQ em níveis vermelhos (ver aqui). No período de 16 a 18 de setembro, no que diz respeito às partículas PM2.5 e PM10, o nosso sistema de monitorização local também registou valores máximos com uma das estações que se localiza fora do centro da cidade, a estação das Taipas, a registar o valor mais alto registado em Guimarães. Embora os outros parâmetros não tenham registado um grande aumento durante o período dos incêndios rurais (O3 e NO2), apresentam ligeiros aumentos durante este período, o que demonstra o impacto dos incêndios rurais na qualidade do ar em geral. A análise dos gráficos de temperatura e temperatura mostra que, durante o período de incêndios, as temperaturas atingiram valores elevados (> 30ºC) e, simultaneamente, os valores de humidade atingiram registos mínimos.

column19: En Côte d'Ivoire, la gestion et la sécurité sanitaire liée à la pollution atmosphérique revet un grand interêt . Dans ce même élan de gestion de la qualité de l'air l'OMS a fixé un seuil d'émission que les pays doivent intégrer dans leur mode de gestion. Cependant, dans les villes de grandes concentrations comme Abidjan il est parfois difficile de maitriser les paramètres d'émissions. L'objectif de cette étude est donc d'estimer les concentrations des polluants atmospreriques particulaires PM2.5 et ensuite cartographier la dynamique de ces polluants de 2015 à 2020. Pour atteindre cet objectif , les données de l'imagerie satellitaire LANDSAT ont été utilisées. Il a s'agit de calculer les réflectances de surfaces et les réflectances au sommet de l'atmosphère. Le but de ces calculs était de déduire les réflectances atmosphériques. En considérant la relation étroite existence entre les PM2.5 et la réflectance atmosphérique un modèle de régression linéaire a été conidéré pour déduire les PM2.5. Les résultats ont montré que les concentrations des PM2.5 sont de façon générale au-dessus du seuil de l'OMS. Ces valeurs sont de 31 μg/m3 en janvier 2015 , de 36 μg/m3 en janvier 2016 , de 32 μg/m3 en décembre 2016, de 33 μg/m3 en janvier 2019 et de 33 μg/m3 en janvier 2020. Cela donne une concentration moyenne de 33 μg/m3. Les communes de Yopougon Nord, Abobo Ouest, Cocody ouest et Port-Bouet Est sont les zones les plus pollués avec des concentrations allant de 26 à 49 μg/m3 .

column19:
The 14 automatic monitors are supplemented by 90 low cost sensors strategically located across the region. Data provided is still that from the WM-Air 2019 (business as usual) model output. The model is currently being updated to provide a 2024 baseline, however was not ready at the time of reporting. Data from the low cost sensor network has also not been included. This is because they are not reportable under LAQM regs (as they are indicative), and due to only recording data from January 2025 we cannot yet derive an annual mean from the data. 

The following paragraph gives wider context to the annual mean presented in 4.9.2.
 
The 'average' annual mean concentrations for NO2 and PM2.5 were calculated by analysing the WM-Air 2019 (business as usual) model output TIFFs and calculating the mean value. The WM-Air model is a validated regional air quality model which covers the whole WMCA area and therefore provides a more representative picture of regional average concentrations in comparison to monitoring. Typically, statutory monitoring will be concentrated in areas of poor air quality and then any background sites will provide a picture of the minimum concentrations. Given the uneven distribution of monitoring locations and the relatively low granularity of automatic monitoring locations across the WMCA area, the modelled estimates provide a more realistic average value across the region. It should be noted that there are limitations with air quality models (likewise with monitoring) and the 'real-world' concentration (as with monitoring) will vary at locations where there is relevant exposure and is dependant on distance to pollutant sources etc. The 7 constituent LAs have at least 14 locations where both NO2 and PM2.5 is monitored using reference/reference equivalent automatic analysers. and it does not include the national AURN/Defra locations which are not typically managed by the LAs.

column19:
Air quality in the City of Balanga is shaped by rapid urbanization, rising transport activity, and growing energy demand. At present, the city has no dedicated continuous air quality monitoring stations, and therefore relies on proxy data from the DENR-EMB regional monitoring network in Central Luzon and the results of its 2018 Climate and Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA), which included a greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions inventory.

The transport sector is the single largest source of air pollution, contributing nearly 79% of the city's total GHG emissions (144,265 tCO₂e in 2018). Aside from carbon dioxide, mobile sources also release particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), black carbon, nitrogen oxides (NOₓ), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), all of which are linked to respiratory and cardiovascular health risks. Traffic congestion in the city's urban core further aggravates localized air quality, particularly during peak commuting hours.

Solid waste decomposition and open burning are additional contributors to poor air quality. The city generates about 65-70 tons of waste per day, with more than half being biodegradable. When unmanaged, this produces methane and nitrous oxide, along with odors and smoke that worsen ambient conditions. In 2018, the waste sector accounted for 33,633 tCO₂e, or 18% of Balanga's total emissions, a significant share that highlights the air quality risks associated with landfill gas and improper disposal practices.

The contribution from electricity use is smaller at 5,043 tCO₂e (3% of total emissions), but because the city's supply is tied to the national grid, which is still heavily dependent on coal-fired generation, local electricity demand indirectly contributes to pollutants such as sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and fine particulates released at the source of generation.

Although Balanga lacks localized monitoring, estimates indicate that PM2.5 concentrations occasionally approach or exceed safe thresholds during periods of high vehicle activity and waste burning. This places sensitive populations—including children, the elderly, and those with respiratory conditions—at greater health risk.

The absence of a city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) station underscores the need for enhanced monitoring and policy action. By promoting sustainable transport, renewable energy adoption, stricter waste management, and green spaces, Balanga can improve both air quality and climate resilience.
